dialogueEnhancement.yourDraft:
"I don't like you," Jackie said.
"I don't like you either," Nick replied.
myOptions:
OPTION 1: More subtext - "Your kind of music is garbage," Jackie said, not looking up from his piano.
"Funny, I was thinking the same thing about yours," Nick said, fingers tight on his guitar strap.

OPTION 2: Class tension - "You wouldn't understand," Jackie said, voice tight with something that wasn't quite anger.
"Try me, rich boy," Nick said. "I'm smarter than I look."

OPTION 3: Musical metaphor - "You play like you're afraid to make mistakes," Jackie said.
"You play like you've never made one," Nick shot back.

sceneBuilding.yourOutline: Nick walks into Jackie's house for the first time
myCollaboration: OPTION 1: Focus on class contrast - Nick's boots tracked dirt onto white carpet he'd never seen outside magazines. Everything in Jackie's house looked breakable—crystal vases, leather couches, and Jackie himself, standing in the doorway like Nick had brought the plague.

OPTION 2: Focus on Nick's emotions - The house smelled like money—furniture polish and something expensive Nick couldn't name. His mother's entire house could fit in Jackie's living room. He forced his hands into his pockets to keep from touching anything.

OPTION 3: Focus on musical connection - The grand piano dominated the room like a black whale. Nick had never seen one in a house before—only in school auditoriums and funeral homes. His fingers itched to touch the keys, but Jackie's expression said don't even think about it.

keyStrengths: I SHOW, NOT JUST TELL. Every suggestion comes with actual rewritten prose you can use or adapt. I never just say 'make it better' - I show you 2-3 ways to make it better, then you choose.

default.description: Collaborative and supportive with multiple creative options. Balances respect for your voice with suggestions for improvement. Focuses on enhancement without judgment of original draft.

nice.description: Encouraging and enthusiastic collaboration. Emphasizes what's already working in your draft. Gentle suggestions framed as 'building on your strengths.' Ideal for early drafts when you need creative confidence.

professional.description: Professional editor collaboration - direct and honest. Points out what's not working and provides better alternatives. BUT ALSO highlights what IS working well so you know your strengths. Focuses on publication-ready quality with complete transparency. Example: 'This dialogue is flat' followed by 'Here's why and here are 3 better options.'
